_meta.description: S4 inference proposals — HYPOTHESES, sourcing-gated. NEVER auto-promoted; review + source + promote by hand.

sibc.against: Industry (Micro and Small, Medium and Large)

sibc.entity: Advances against Fixed Deposits (Including FCNR (B), NRNR Deposits etc.)

proposals.label: Rural water/sanitation scheme capex drives social-infrastructure contractor credit
proposals.mechanism: A step-up in central-scheme fund release for drinking water and sanitation works increases working-capital and project credit draw by social-infrastructure contractors and implementing agencies.
proposals.required_source: Jal Jeevan Mission (ejalshakti.gov.in) fund-release and utilisation dashboard for the quarter in question
source_ladder: Jal Jeevan Mission / Swachh Bharat Mission dashboard: fund-release and utilisation report for the period
PIB press release, Ministry of Jal Shakti, on fund releases to states for the period
Union Budget / Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation demand-for-grants document showing the allocation and release schedule

attempts.target: Jal Jeevan Mission (ejalshakti.gov.in) fund-release and utilisation dashboard for the quarter in question
attempts.note: verified via editor browser (host refuses automated reads)
attempts.editor_note: Not promoted by editor decision (2026-11-13). Official and verified, but it does not fit the September move: most of the release (₹5,289 cr) reimburses states for work already paid from their own funds, which would let contractors repay credit rather than draw it; JJM 2.0 was approved on 10 Mar 2026, too early for a one-month jump; Social Infrastructure is a small line where one loan can move +186 pp.

proposals.label: BIS Quality Control Order forces compliance-driven output cut at glass units
proposals.mechanism: A BIS Quality Control Order mandating certification for glass and glassware products forces non-compliant (mostly SME) units to halt or cut production, reducing their short-term credit draw relative to the broader industry cut.
proposals.required_source: BIS Quality Control Order gazette notification for glass/glassware products
source_ladder: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) Quality Control Order gazette notification for glass/glassware, with its compliance deadline
DPIIT press release or circular implementing/extending the QCO
Trade press (Glass Global, FICCI glass-industry note, or Business Standard) on unit closures/output cuts tied to the QCO deadline

attempts.target: BIS Quality Control Order for glass/glassware with a compliance date in the window
attempts.note: Searched 2026-11-13 ('BIS Quality Control Order glass glassware 2026'; BIS 'Upcoming QCOs notified and due for implementation'): no glass or glassware QCO in force around Sep 2026. The only glass item is Glass Screen Protector (IS 19348:2025), enforcement 1 Apr 2027; the Laboratory Glassware QCO dates from 2023.

proposals.label: Red Sea route disruption cuts Indian shipping line credit draw
proposals.mechanism: Red Sea/Suez route diversion and the resulting freight-rate volatility reduce cargo volumes and revenue for Indian shipping lines, cutting their working-capital and vessel-financing credit draw.
proposals.required_source: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways / DG Shipping press release on route disruption impact, or Baltic Exchange freight index for the period
source_ladder: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (DG Shipping) press release or circular addressing Red Sea route disruption impact on Indian shipping
Baltic Exchange Baltic Dry Index / Baltic Dirty Tanker Index data for the period
Financial/trade press (Lloyd's List, Mint, Business Standard) report on Indian shipping line freight revenue and borrowing for the period

attempts.target: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways / DG Shipping release on Red Sea disruption affecting Indian shipping
attempts.note: Searched 2026-11-13 ('Indian shipping companies September 2026 freight Red Sea DG Shipping'): only DGS maritime security advisories for seafarers (Orders/Circulars 41, 42 of 2026), not credit-relevant. Press (unverified) reports MSC and Maersk resuming selected Red Sea services in late Aug/early Sep 2026, the opposite direction. Shipping has few borrowers; one large repayment may explain -20 pp.

proposals.label: Interest-subvention season pulls forward crop-loan disbursal
proposals.mechanism: A revised or expanded Modified Interest Subvention Scheme rate/coverage for the Kharif season lowers effective crop-loan borrowing cost, pulling disbursal forward into September.
proposals.required_source: RBI/NABARD circular on the Interest Subvention Scheme for Short Term Crop Loans for the current season
source_ladder: RBI Master Direction / circular on the Interest Subvention Scheme (ISS/MISS) for the current crop season
NABARD circular to banks on MISS claim and disbursement guidelines for the season
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare press release (PIB) on Kharif crop-loan targets and subvention coverage

attempts.target: RBI/NABARD circular on the Interest Subvention Scheme for the 2026 kharif season
attempts.note: Searched 2026-11-13 ('Modified Interest Subvention Scheme 2026-27 short term crop loans RBI circular'): the latest RBI MISS circular is 13 Jan 2026 (for 2025-26, continued without changes); no 2026-27 change found. The new KCC Directions (RBI, 19 Jun 2026) apply from 1 Jan 2027, after the window. An unchanged scheme cannot explain a sudden move.

proposals.label: Festive-season bank campaigns push loans against fixed deposits
proposals.mechanism: Banks' festive-season promotional campaigns (preferential rates, instant digital sanction) on overdrafts/loans against fixed deposits pull borrowers from unsecured personal loans toward FD-backed credit.
proposals.required_source: Bank press release on a festive-season loan-against-FD or instant digital OD-against-deposit offer
source_ladder: Individual bank (SBI/HDFC/ICICI) press release announcing a festive-season loan/OD-against-FD offer or digital instant-sanction launch
RBI Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies referencing digital lending or deposit-backed credit facilities
Financial press (Economic Times, Mint) coverage of bank festive-season loan campaigns for the period

proposals.label: Food-procurement credit timing shifts the non-food/total mix
proposals.mechanism: A timing shift in FCI/state-agency foodgrain procurement cash-credit drawdown changes the food-credit component's weight inside total bank credit, nudging the non-food share even with no change in underlying non-food lending.
proposals.required_source: FCI procurement progress report / RBI food-credit line for the period
source_ladder: Food Corporation of India procurement progress report for the marketing season
RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement, food credit line, for the period
PIB press release on foodgrain procurement (Kharif/Rabi marketing season) progress

triage.note: food credit is our own series: a change in the food/non-food mix is composition, not an external cause; the Non-food move is +0.07 pp against a tiny usual change

proposals.label: AePS/micro-ATM cash-out growth → debit-card POS cash withdrawal substitution
proposals.mechanism: Aadhaar-enabled micro-ATM and bank-mitra cash-out points let customers pull cash without swiping a debit card at a merchant terminal, diverting spend away from DC POS cash withdrawal.
source_ladder: NPCI AePS product statistics page (npci.org.in/statistics)
RBI Payment System Indicators / Annual Report chapter on AEPS and Business Correspondent network
Named financial press report (e.g. BusinessLine, Economic Times) on AePS/micro-ATM cash-out growth

proposals.label: Card-on-file tokenisation mandate → card e-commerce decline
proposals.mechanism: RBI's CoF tokenisation requirement forced merchants to delete stored card numbers, adding checkout friction that pushed card-based online spend toward UPI/wallets.
source_ladder: RBI master direction/FAQ: 'Tokenisation – Card Transactions: Permitting Card-on-File Tokenisation (CoFT) Services'
RBI Payment and Settlement Systems annual report commentary on tokenisation's transition impact
Named financial press report on tokenisation's effect on card e-commerce volumes

triage.note: card-on-file tokenisation took effect 1 Oct 2022 (RBI CoFT deadline); four years before the Sep 2026 window, too old to explain a sudden move

proposals.label: Merchant category code reclassification → debit 'other' spend inflation
proposals.mechanism: A card-network or RBI reclassification of merchant category codes moved transactions previously booked under POS or e-commerce into the residual 'other' bucket, inflating it without a real behaviour shift.
proposals.required_source: RBI/NPCI payment system statistics definitions note or card-network MCC bulletin
source_ladder: RBI Payment System Indicators methodology/definitions note
NPCI or card network (Visa/Mastercard/RuPay) MCC classification circular
Named financial press report on card transaction reclassification

proposals.label: RuPay/Jan Dhan debit card issuance drive → debit card spend volume growth
proposals.mechanism: Continued PSU-bank issuance of RuPay debit cards under Jan Dhan accounts adds a high-frequency, low-ticket transaction base that grows debit card spend volume faster than value.
proposals.required_source: PMJDY progress report / RuPay debit card issuance data
source_ladder: PMJDY official progress dashboard (pmjdy.gov.in)
RBI/NPCI RuPay card issuance and usage statistics
Named financial press report on Jan Dhan debit card issuance drive

proposals.label: Issuer-specific RBI supervisory restriction on new credit card onboarding → credit card spend value decline
proposals.mechanism: An RBI supervisory order barring a major issuer from onboarding new credit card customers removes new-card spend growth from the base, pulling down aggregate credit card spend value.
proposals.required_source: RBI press release naming the restricted issuer and the onboarding ban
source_ladder: RBI press release/circular on the specific issuer restriction
RBI Annual Report / Trend and Progress of Banking in India chapter on supervisory actions
Named financial press report on the restriction's business impact

proposals.label: Co-branded credit card programme discontinuation → credit card e-commerce volume decline
proposals.mechanism: Discontinuation or downgrade of a high-volume co-branded e-commerce credit card partnership removes a large recurring slice of online transaction volume.
proposals.required_source: Issuer or partner press release/investor disclosure announcing the co-brand programme's discontinuation
source_ladder: Issuer/partner press release or investor disclosure on the co-brand card discontinuation
RBI Payment System Indicators showing the volume step-down coincident with the announced date
Named financial press report on the partnership's end

proposals.label: EMI conversion of card purchases moves balances off revolving card stock
proposals.mechanism: Issuers let a cardholder convert a large purchase into a fixed-tenure EMI at or soon after the point of sale; once converted, that amount is carried as a personal/consumer loan, not revolving card debt, so the spend counted in ATM/POS value/volume never shows up in SIBC's credit-card outstanding line.
proposals.affects: icl:sibc/Statement1/4.5 vs icl:atm_pos spend_value (credit_card, all channels)
proposals.required_source: RBI Master Direction – Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022 (EMI-conversion disclosure clause)
source_ladder: RBI Master Direction – Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022, EMI-conversion clause
RBI Monthly Bulletin / DBIE 'Loans and Advances' table, if it breaks out EMI-converted card balances separately
Card issuer investor presentation or annual report (e.g. SBI Cards, HDFC Bank) disclosing % of card spend converted to EMI

proposals.label: Co-branded card partnership launch/exit shifts e-com/POS spend mix without moving outstanding
proposals.mechanism: A major bank-merchant co-branded card (e.g. an e-commerce or airline tie-up) being launched or discontinued concentrates spend growth among cardholders who typically pay in full, so e-com/POS credit-card spend value jumps or drops sharply while the revolving outstanding stock barely moves.
proposals.required_source: Issuing bank's press release or stock-exchange disclosure announcing the co-branded card launch or termination
source_ladder: Bank's official press release / exchange filing announcing the co-brand launch or termination
RBI Monthly Bulletin 'Developments in Banking' section, if it names the partnership
Business press report (Economic Times, Mint, Business Standard) quoting the partnership's card issuance or spend numbers

proposals.label: RBI's penal-charge cap reduces the cost of revolving, slowing outstanding growth independent of spend
proposals.mechanism: RBI's rule barring penal charges disguised as interest and capping punitive charges on loan accounts (including credit cards) lowers the cost of carrying a balance, which can slow the growth rate of card outstanding even as transaction spend keeps rising.
proposals.affects: icl:sibc/Statement1/4.5 growth rate vs icl:atm_pos/spend_value (credit_card) growth rate
proposals.required_source: RBI circular 'Fair Lending Practices – Penal Charges in Loan Accounts'
source_ladder: RBI circular 'Fair Lending Practices – Penal Charges in Loan Accounts' (2023/2024)
RBI Master Direction on credit card interest rates/charges, if it cross-references the same clause
Card issuer's revised Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC) document reflecting the lower penal charge

triage.note: RBI penal-charges circular (Aug 2023) applied from 1 Jan 2024 (existing loans by Apr 2024); a standing rule for over two years cannot explain a change in the 2026 window

proposals.label: Non-bank BNPL apps divert e-commerce spend away from bank credit cards
proposals.mechanism: Growth of non-bank Buy-Now-Pay-Later checkout options (not booked in SIBC's bank credit-card outstanding) pulls a share of e-commerce transaction value away from bank-issued credit cards, so recorded credit-card e-com spend growth undershoots what the outstanding-stock trend alone would predict.
proposals.required_source: RBI 'Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India', digital lending/BNPL chapter
source_ladder: RBI 'Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India' (digital lending/BNPL section, relevant year)
RBI Working Group / Guidelines on Digital Lending report
Industry market-sizing report (e.g. Redseer, BCG, RBI-cited third party) on India BNPL transaction value

proposals.label: Card-on-file tokenisation mandate disrupted e-commerce credit-card transaction volume independent of outstanding
proposals.mechanism: RBI's mandate removing stored card-on-file data from merchants and replacing it with tokens caused a transition-period drop (then recovery) in saved-card checkout convenience, moving e-commerce credit-card transaction volume/value for reasons unrelated to any change in revolving outstanding.
proposals.required_source: RBI circular on Card-on-File Tokenisation (CoFT) and its implementation deadline extensions
source_ladder: RBI circular mandating Card-on-File Tokenisation and subsequent deadline-extension circulars
RBI press release / FAQ on CoFT implementation
Payments-industry press report (e.g. on NPCI/Visa/Mastercard token adoption rates) on the transition's effect on e-com checkout volumes

triage.note: same instrument as #7 (CoFT, in force from 1 Oct 2022): outside the window for a stock-flow link judged in 2026

proposals.label: The Shipping Corporation of India refinanced rupee loans with a US$100.4 mn ECB (Sep 2026)
proposals.mechanism: SCI registered a 5-year ECB of US$100.4 mn to refinance rupee loans, from a resident financial institution's branch outside India: debt moves off domestic bank books, so SIBC's Shipping line falls with no change in shipping activity.
proposals.required_source: RBI, Data on ECB/FCCB for the month of September 2026 (borrower list)
source_ladder: RBI ECB borrower list, September 2026 (XLSX/PDF on rbidocs, listed on www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/ECBView.aspx)

attempts.target: RBI, Data on ECB/FCCB for the month of September 2026 (borrower list)
attempts.note: verified via editor browser (host refuses automated reads)
